meta.purpose: Timestamps, counts, units, hints, table data on the board, toast meta.

label.purpose: Names, group headings, badges, chips, small buttons, menu items, segment labels.

body.purpose: Sentences, descriptions, alert text, prose; running text measures 60 to 72ch.

prose.purpose: Transcript prose and rendered markdown, Figtree at 1.55.

title.purpose: Page, dialog and empty-state titles; 18px at 390px to 20px at 1024px.

kpi.purpose: A stat tile's figure, tabular; 20px to 24px, the title size under 900px.

column-head.purpose: A ledger's header band, uppercase, 0.06em tracking.

code.purpose: JetBrains Mono for code, commands, paths, tool names and keycaps; ligatures off.

display.purpose: Fredoka 600, brand display only: marketing, a brand moment in an empty state. Never product chrome; the wordmark is Nunito.

row.purpose: The title of a row that is a thing to read, not a name to scan: a task's linked items.

mono-figure.purpose: A measurement standing among Figtree words: the usage popover's and strip's times, week shares.

shadows.name: shadow-xs
shadows.purpose: Inputs, select triggers, the new-session prompt.

shadows.name: shadow-tile
shadows.value: 0 1px 2px light-dark(oklch(from var(--neutral-12) l c h / 0.07), oklch(0% 0 0 / 0.3)), 0 0 0 1px light-dark(oklch(from var(--neutral-12) l c h / 0.035), oklch(from var(--neutral-12) l c h / 0.06))
shadows.purpose: Cards, tiles, icon tiles, report cards, the fluid-tabs segment.

shadows.name: shadow-raised
shadows.purpose: A thumb in a groove; the night ring edges it at night.

shadows.name: shadow-hairline
shadows.purpose: A drop under a tile with no ring: the stat tile (light), the permission card.

shadows.name: shadow-stat
shadows.purpose: The stat tile's lift: a drop below the card, ringed at night.

shadows.name: shadow-md
shadows.purpose: Tailwind ladder step.

shadows.name: shadow-lg
shadows.purpose: Tailwind ladder step (meters' hover cards).

shadows.name: shadow-xl
shadows.purpose: Tailwind ladder step (project popover, tool matrix).

shadows.name: shadow-overlay
shadows.purpose: Popovers, menus, the dialog tray, toasts, floating tags (also --shadow-modal).

shadows.name: shadow-overlay-hung
shadows.purpose: A hanging surface whose top shows its own surface across the cut into its anchor (Caw's panel, kit-hang): the overlay's drop without the night ring, which would draw across the cut as a seam.

shadows.name: shadow-modal
shadows.purpose: The modal: the overlay value.

shadows.name: shadow-drawer
shadows.purpose: Sheets and drawers.

shadows.name: shadow-drop
shadows.purpose: A drawn shape's drop (the grown composer), drawn as the SVG's own feDropShadow filters so it follows the shape, not a box, and is painted once rather than reapplied as the shape moves (grown.ts): this far layer, then shadow-drop-near.

shadows.name: shadow-drop-near
shadows.purpose: The near layer of a drawn shape's drop, under shadow-drop (the grown composer, once it stands still).

shadows.name: shadow-tab-start
shadows.purpose: A folder tab's edge on the tab behind it, at its leading side: one-sided, never above its top (PaneTabs .shade).

shadows.name: shadow-tab-end
shadows.purpose: A folder tab's edge on the tab behind it, at its trailing side (PaneTabs .shade).

shadows.name: shadow-tab-start-chosen
shadows.purpose: The chosen folder tab's edge on the tab behind it, at its leading side (PaneTabs .shade).

shadows.name: shadow-tab-end-chosen
shadows.purpose: The chosen folder tab's edge on the tab behind it, at its trailing side (PaneTabs .shade).

shadows.name: shadow-inset-sel
shadows.purpose: A selected control sunk into its field (markdown editor).

shadows.name: action-ring
shadows.purpose: The action's edge: a white top hairline and a coral-tinted drop.

shadows.name: code-ring
shadows.purpose: Inner vermillion ring and soft inner glow on code blocks.

shadows.name: shadow-knob
shadows.value: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--neutral-8), 0 1px 3px var(--shadow-tint), 0 1px 1px var(--shadow-tint), inset 0 0 0 1px var(--night-ring)
shadows.purpose: The effort knob's and Browse's lifted block: a neutral-8 inner edge over shadow-raised's layers (DESIGN.md Effort chip).

shadows.name: shadow-tint
shadows.value: light-dark(oklch(from var(--neutral-12) l c h / 0.09), oklch(from var(--neutral-1) l c h / 0.55))
shadows.purpose: Elevation tints: warm ink by day, the deepest surface at night, never rgba black.

shadows.name: shadow-tint-2
shadows.value: light-dark(oklch(from var(--neutral-12) l c h / 0.14), oklch(from var(--neutral-1) l c h / 0.66))
shadows.purpose: Second shadow tint.

shadows.name: shadow-tint-3
shadows.value: light-dark(oklch(from var(--neutral-12) l c h / 0.2), oklch(from var(--neutral-1) l c h / 0.76))
shadows.purpose: Third shadow tint, for overlays and drawers.

shadows.name: night-ring
shadows.value: light-dark(transparent, oklch(from var(--neutral-12) l c h / 0.07))
shadows.purpose: At night every raised shadow adds a 1px inner ring of ink.

shadows.name: scrim
shadows.value: oklch(from var(--background) l c h / var(--scrim-mix))
shadows.purpose: What a dialog's backdrop paints: the page itself, translucent.

shadows.name: material-panel
shadows.purpose: Chrome materials: structural translucency, never decoration.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Entrances, exits, colour and any change in place: the default.

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: Things already on screen moving from one place to another, and a figure filling to a new value: rows sliding, thumbs gliding, height tweens, a usage arc, a strategy figure's lane.

motion.name: ease-drawer
motion.purpose: Floating surfaces, sheets, page swaps, shared-element flights, container size changes.

motion.name: ease-crossfade
motion.purpose: The owner's one gentle curve, bound to the skeleton's pulse and reveal and a folder tab's choice over dur-settle: beats of 400ms and longer. At most 7.2% of a change in any 1/60s at 400ms.

motion.name: ease-goo
motion.purpose: The one overshoot in the product, bound to a comment card pouring out of its pin (PinFloat). A shape pouring out of another as one drawn silhouette (goo-join): a comment's card out of its pill. It overshoots a little and settles, the liquid's give. transitions.dev Gooey plus menu, its open curve (--pv3i).

motion.name: ease-glide-out
motion.purpose: The last stretch of a steady glide; the glide starts at speed. From the steady pace, speed falling evenly to rest. Only glide() in motion/curves.svelte.ts writes it; no component picks it.

motion.name: dur-stagger
motion.purpose: Between one row of an opening tree and the next: its line reaches each glyph in turn at a steady pace.

motion.name: dur-type
motion.purpose: Between one letter of a typed example and the next: New project's placeholder typing its examples once, then resting; it erases at half this.

motion.name: dur-cascade
motion.purpose: The most an opening tree's line takes to reach its last row: a longer tree's rows come closer together.

motion.name: dur-ghost
motion.purpose: The hover ghost gliding from row to row.

motion.name: dur-control
motion.purpose: Control colour changes, cross-fades, glyph swaps, reduced-motion page fade.

motion.name: dur-menu
motion.purpose: Tooltips, content fading into an opened place, a new thinking step.

motion.name: dur-peek
motion.purpose: How long the pointer rests on a comment's pill before its peek comes, one within this of the last coming at once; and how long the peek stays once the pointer has left the pill and the peek (DESIGN.md, A pin's pill).

motion.name: dur-toggle
motion.purpose: A switch's knob, a checkbox's tick drawing, a step connector drawing.

motion.name: dur-exit
motion.purpose: Every exit: popovers, dialogs, sheets, toasts, floating tags, row fades.

motion.name: dur-morph
motion.purpose: A button's width following its label while it works; folding a long draft.

motion.name: dur-rail
motion.purpose: A transcript row's place opening, its rail drawing down with it.

motion.name: dur-fade
motion.purpose: Fades that carry state in place: the theme wash, a toast stack closing up.

motion.name: dur-mark-hold
motion.purpose: The longest a transcript that opens on a compaction holds its reveal for Caw's mark to be drawn. A bound, not a pace.

motion.name: dur-wait-grace
motion.purpose: How long a wait runs before its loading state (Caw at loading or reconnecting) appears; a shorter wait shows its plain surface. NN/g, Response Times: no special feedback is needed for delays under 1.0 second.

motion.name: dur-pop
motion.purpose: Floating surfaces opening, list arrivals, the live tail's height tween.

motion.name: dur-panel
motion.purpose: Dialogs and sheets entering, list movement, toasts rising, badge tint changes.

motion.name: dur-panel-exit
motion.purpose: A panel the width of the sidebar leaving on --ease-drawer, the curve it came in on: shorter than --dur-panel (The Fast Exit Rule), long enough that its slide reads as one motion.

motion.name: dur-pick-up
motion.purpose: A pane card picked up off the deck: the lift's scale, sixty percent of the panel's beat, derived from it the way the breath is.

motion.name: dur-grow
motion.purpose: The composer growing up out of its pill: into the recall wheel, or by the one row that says a queued message is being edited.

motion.name: dur-grow-exit
motion.purpose: The grown composer folding back into its pill, shorter than its growth.

motion.name: dur-goo
motion.purpose: A comment's card pouring out of its pill as one silhouette, on --ease-goo. transitions.dev Gooey plus menu, its open (--pv3x).

motion.name: dur-goo-exit
motion.purpose: A comment's card drawn back into its pill as one silhouette, on --ease-out, shorter than its open. transitions.dev Gooey plus menu, its close (--pv3g).

motion.name: dur-goo-content
motion.purpose: What stands on a goo shape fading in, on --ease-out after --dur-goo-content-delay. transitions.dev Gooey plus menu, its items' icons in (180ms; their 2px blur is left out: a transitioned filter can hang WebKit).

motion.name: dur-goo-content-delay
motion.purpose: How long what stands on a goo shape waits as the shape pours out before it resolves in: the shape has most of its room by then. transitions.dev Gooey plus menu, its items' icons (+120ms).

motion.name: dur-goo-content-exit
motion.purpose: What stands on a goo shape fading out as the shape drains, at once, on --ease-out. transitions.dev Gooey plus menu, its items' icons out (120ms).

motion.name: dur-goo-settle
motion.purpose: The dip a goo shape's anchor takes as what poured out of it drains back: down --goo-dip at 30% and home, on --ease-out. A comment's pin as its card closes. transitions.dev Gooey plus menu, its anticipation (--pv2w).

motion.name: dur-lift
motion.purpose: A queued message's words flying between its bubble and the composer field, either way, two copies crossfading on the drawer curve.

motion.name: dur-press-hold
motion.purpose: How long a touch rests on the composer, keyboard down, before the recall wheel comes up under it.

motion.name: dur-settle
motion.purpose: The existing motion/spring.ts response for non-paging surface settlement. Paging uses UIScrollView's system mechanics. Also a folder tab's choice, on ease-crossfade (the owner's pick, "Slow · 400ms").

motion.name: dur-glide
motion.purpose: A tab track's glide under a mouse wheel: the second spring's response.

motion.name: dur-hold
motion.purpose: How long a done state (a copied or saved check) stays up.

motion.name: dur-loop
motion.purpose: One turn of an ambient loop while something is pending: spinners, the task ring, and Tailwind's animate-spin (linear), animate-pulse (ease-in-out) and animate-ping (ease-out). The skeleton pulses on its own --dur-skeleton-pulse (1s), transitions.dev's recipe.

motion.name: dur-skeleton-pulse
motion.purpose: One pulse of a skeleton while it waits: its opacity from 1 down to --skeleton-pulse-floor and back, on --ease-crossfade, looping until what it stands for arrives. transitions.dev Skeleton loader and reveal, --pulse-dur: 1000ms (the owner's pick: "transitions.dev exactly").

motion.name: dur-skeleton-reveal
motion.purpose: A skeleton handing its place to what it stood for: the skeleton fades out and blurs to --skeleton-reveal-blur while the content fades in out of it, both on --ease-crossfade. transitions.dev Skeleton loader and reveal, --reveal-dur: 400ms.

motion.name: breath
motion.purpose: The opacity pulse of live work: beats, the in-flight tool glyph, the Working glyph, shimmer.

motion.name: press-scale
motion.purpose: Every press scale, over --dur-toggle on ease-out; also the new-session dialog's exit scale and the phone deck's pick-up.

motion.name: leave-scale
motion.purpose: How far Caw shrinks as he fades out, from any drawing, over --dur-fade on ease-out, and the size a Caw whose status has no drawn enter fades in from, over --dur-pop. Material 3, Easing and duration: exit transitions are faster than enters, 200ms.

motion.name: pop-scale
motion.purpose: The scale a floating surface, chip or pop grows from and shrinks to.

motion.name: deck-step
motion.purpose: How far each card of a session mark's deck shows below the one in front (SessionMark).

motion.name: deck-shrink
motion.purpose: How much smaller each deck card is than the one in front: card i is the tile scaled by 1 - 0.11 x i.

motion.name: deck-shade-step
motion.purpose: How much more of the deck's shade each card behind takes.

motion.name: echo-scale
motion.purpose: How far a working session's echo grows from its tile before it has faded (motion/echo).

motion.name: echo-opacity
motion.purpose: A working session's echo as it leaves the tile.

motion.name: breath-floor
motion.purpose: The opacity live work breathes down to, half a breath in (the shared `breath` keyframes, app.css). The lowest at which every breather's ink (the status-live glyph, each tool family's ink, the muted ink) holds 3:1 (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11, unrounded) on every surface it stands on: page, raised, recess, recess-deep and well (probe breath-and-head). By day 0.8 (the search tool's ink on recess-deep the floor, 3.13:1); at night 0.58 (the plan tool's ink on raised the floor, 3.14:1).

motion.name: account-week-mix
motion.purpose: How far an account's week rim is mixed from its hue toward account-week-toward: a clearly different lightness of the same hue. By day 0.32 (the rim 1.9:1 or more from the disc); at night 0.63, the lowest at which the rim stands 1.8:1 from the disc for every account hue (rose the floor), the rim then 7.9:1 or more on its track.

motion.name: account-stale-opacity
motion.purpose: An account whose reading is out of date: its rings and its relay band draw at this opacity, the lowest at which every account hue holds 3:1 against the border-control track it lies on, in both schemes (by day cyan and green set the floor at 0.82, at night rose at 0.80); on the raised surface they hold more.

motion.name: ride-fade
motion.purpose: The first stretch of its nesting line over which a child's icon fades in as it leaves its parent's (motion/branch).

motion.name: pop-rise
motion.purpose: How far every surface, row or part travels as it comes or goes (The Enter Rule): a floating surface or toast from its edge, a list swap's rows sideways, a keyframe's rise.

motion.name: tip-rise
motion.purpose: How far a tooltip settles toward its trigger as it fades in: The Enter Rule's one exception, short because it is seen tens of times a day (The Frequency Rule).

motion.name: swap-nudge
motion.purpose: How far a view handing its place to the next along a strip travels as it comes in or goes: a tab switch's transcript and its composer's words, from the side of the tab it came from. A cue of which way it went, not a page turn.

motion.name: fold-blur
motion.purpose: How soft a fold's content is while it folds shut or opens (Caw's panel: the update's notes, the logins signed in everywhere). transitions-dev Accordion expand: the inner panel cross-blurs 2px as its grid row goes 0fr to 1fr.

motion.name: part-blur
motion.purpose: How far out of focus the grown composer's parts come up from, and sink back into as it folds: an ask card's title, body and foot; the queued edit's label, hints and Keep it. Web only.

motion.name: goo-join
motion.purpose: Where a goo shape meets what poured out of it (a comment's pin and its card): the radius every inward corner of the one silhouette is rounded to, so the join flares out along the card's edge and the two read as one shape. A card's own corner, so the flare and the corners are one curve family.

motion.name: goo-dip
motion.purpose: How far a goo shape's anchor dips as what poured out of it drains back, over --dur-goo-settle. transitions.dev Gooey plus menu (--pv49: 5px).

motion.name: skeleton-pulse-floor
motion.purpose: The opacity a skeleton pulses down to, half a pulse in. transitions.dev Skeleton loader and reveal, --pulse-min: 0.5.

motion.name: skeleton-reveal-blur
motion.purpose: How soft a skeleton is as it goes and its content as it comes, at the far end of the reveal's cross-fade. transitions.dev Skeleton loader and reveal, --reveal-blur: 2px.

motion.name: transition-control
motion.value: background-color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), border-color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), --tw-gradient-from var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), --tw-gradient-to var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: The default control transition.

motion.name: transition-fade-show
motion.purpose: Something stepping back in: its fade, and its visibility back at once (the composer's prompts, slots and controls when an ask lets go).

motion.name: transition-fade-hide
motion.value: opacity var(--dur-fade) var(--ease-out), visibility 0s linear var(--dur-fade)
motion.purpose: Something stepping aside: its fade, and its visibility gone once the fade is done (the composer's parts under an ask, a drawing, a minimized pill).

motion.name: transition-exit-show
motion.purpose: The composer's tray coming back: the exit's beat, its visibility back at once.

motion.name: transition-exit-hide
motion.value: opacity var(--dur-exit) var(--ease-out), visibility 0s linear var(--dur-exit)
motion.purpose: The composer's tray leaving: the exit's beat, its visibility gone once the fade is done.

motion.name: transition-fade-blur
motion.value: opacity var(--dur-fade) var(--ease-out), filter var(--dur-fade) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: A part fading up out of a slight blur (part-blur) in place, with reduced motion: an ask card's title, body and foot; the queued edit's label, hints and Keep it. Tested in iOS 27.2 Safari on 2026-10-23 (probe-kit ios-safari-motion): the page answers through it and the blur runs.

motion.name: transition-fade-slide-blur
motion.value: opacity var(--dur-fade) var(--ease-out), translate var(--dur-panel) var(--ease-drawer), filter var(--dur-fade) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: A part fading up out of a slight blur (part-blur) as it slides into place on the drawer curve: an ask card's title, body and foot; the queued edit's label, hints and Keep it. Tested in iOS 27.2 Safari on 2026-10-23 (probe-kit ios-safari-motion): the page answers through it and the blur runs.

motion.name: transition-tint-press
motion.value: background-color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), transform var(--dur-toggle) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: A chip's fill and ink on the control's beat, and its press scale (transform) on the toggle's (the tree's count, a needs card's chip, a notice row).

motion.name: transition-control-press
motion.value: background-color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), border-color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), --tw-gradient-from var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), --tw-gradient-to var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), transform var(--dur-toggle) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: transition-control, and the press's transform on the toggle's beat.

motion.name: transition-control-slide
motion.value: background-color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), border-color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), translate var(--dur-exit) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: transition-control, and a swiped row's translate home on the exit's beat.

motion.name: transition-control-ring
motion.value: background-color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), border-color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), box-shadow var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: transition-control, and a ring drawn as a box-shadow on the same beat.

motion.name: transition-chip-settle
motion.value: background-color var(--dur-panel) var(--ease-out), color var(--dur-panel) var(--ease-out), transform var(--dur-toggle) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: A chip whose fill and ink settle on the panel's beat, its press (transform) on the toggle's (a rollout's state chip).

motion.name: transition-pick-card
motion.value: border-color var(--dur-fade) var(--ease-out), background-color var(--dur-fade) var(--ease-out), transform var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: A choice card's outline and fill on the fade's beat, its press (transform) on the control's (the account strategy picker).

motion.name: transition-frame-end-first
motion.value: inset-inline-end var(--dur-fade) var(--ease-in-out) 0ms, inset-inline-start var(--dur-fade) var(--ease-in-out) var(--dur-ghost)
motion.purpose: A frame gliding between cards: its leading edge moves at once, its trailing edge a ghost's beat later, so it stretches then settles (the channel cards).

motion.name: transition-frame-start-first
motion.value: inset-inline-start var(--dur-fade) var(--ease-in-out) 0ms, inset-inline-end var(--dur-fade) var(--ease-in-out) var(--dur-ghost)
motion.purpose: transition-frame-end-first's mirror, for a glide the other way.

motion.name: transition-split-surface
motion.value: opacity var(--dur-panel) var(--ease-out), transform var(--dur-panel) var(--ease-out), padding var(--dur-panel) var(--ease-drawer)
motion.purpose: A side surface sliding in beside the main pane: its fade and travel on ease-out, its room (padding) on the drawer curve.

motion.name: transition-ring-arc
motion.value: stroke-dashoffset var(--dur-panel) var(--ease-in-out), stroke var(--dur-toggle) var(--ease-out), opacity var(--dur-toggle) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: A usage ring's arc drawing to its new length, its stroke and fade on the toggle's beat.

motion.name: transition-rail-tip
motion.value: transform var(--dur-morph) var(--ease-in-out), width var(--dur-morph) var(--ease-in-out), opacity var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: A rail's selection tip gliding and resizing to its new item, fading on the control's beat.

motion.name: transition-panel-travel
motion.value: transform var(--dur-panel) var(--ease-in-out), opacity var(--dur-panel) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: A panel travelling to its new place on ease-in-out while it fades on ease-out (the new-session location panels).

motion.name: transition-panel-resize
motion.value: transform var(--dur-toggle) var(--ease-in-out), height var(--dur-toggle) var(--ease-in-out), opacity var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: A panel moving and taking its new height on the toggle's beat, fading on the control's (the model list's panel).

motion.name: transition-suggest-chip
motion.value: scale var(--dur-toggle) var(--ease-out), background-color var(--dur-panel) var(--ease-out), border-color var(--dur-panel) var(--ease-out), color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: A suggestion chip: its press on the toggle's beat, its tint and outline on the panel's, its ink on the control's.

motion.name: transition-segment
motion.value: transform var(--dur-toggle) var(--ease-out), width var(--dur-toggle) var(--ease-out), height var(--dur-toggle) var(--ease-out), opacity var(--dur-ghost) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: A segmented control's thumb gliding and resizing to its tab, fading on the ghost's beat.

motion.name: transition-fold-fade
motion.value: opacity var(--dur-exit) var(--ease-out), filter var(--dur-exit) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: A fold's inner panel fading and cross-blurring out of --fold-blur as it opens and shuts (UpdateCard, MovedLogins, RecordCard; the open state stretches it to the panel's beat). A transitioned filter can hang WebKit; these folds are each driven on WebKit by scripts/probe-kit/specs/web/safari-blurs.ts, so no other element takes this.

motion.name: transition-band-hide
motion.value: opacity var(--dur-exit) var(--ease-out), visibility var(--dur-exit) linear, background-color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: The connection band (HubBand) going, with less motion: its fade and its visibility on the exit's beat, its tint and ink on the control's.

motion.name: transition-band-show
motion.value: opacity var(--dur-panel) var(--ease-drawer), visibility var(--dur-panel) linear, background-color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: The connection band (HubBand) coming, with less motion: its fade and its visibility on the panel's beat and the drawer curve, its tint and ink on the control's.

motion.name: transition-band-slide-hide
motion.value: translate var(--dur-exit) var(--ease-out), opacity var(--dur-exit) var(--ease-out), visibility var(--dur-exit) linear, background-color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: The connection band (HubBand) going back up under the bar: its travel, fade and visibility on the exit's beat, its tint and ink on the control's.

motion.name: transition-band-slide-show
motion.value: translate var(--dur-panel) var(--ease-drawer), opacity var(--dur-panel) var(--ease-drawer), visibility var(--dur-panel) linear, background-color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out), color var(--dur-control) var(--ease-out)
motion.purpose: The connection band (HubBand) sliding down from under the bar: its travel, fade and visibility on the panel's beat and the drawer curve, its tint and ink on the control's.

motion.name: transition-band-row-shut
motion.purpose: The connection band's row (HubBand) shutting as the band goes back up: its grid row on the exit's beat.

motion.name: transition-band-row-open

narrative.northStar: The Quiet Ledger, re-skinned for Caw&Co
narrative.overview:
CawCo is a board an operator glances at between other work, to answer one question: does anything need me right now? It reads like a departure board: rows hold still, numbers line up, and a quiet row means a healthy row.

The surface is warm paper by day and roost-dark at night, low in chroma. Colour is spent on five things only: the coral action, status, identity marks, the focus ring, and data past a threshold. Depth is a recessed frame holding raised content. Neither scheme is the original: every colour token picks its side through `light-dark()`, and a design is drawn and checked in both.
keyCharacteristics: A coral action on warm paper; colour elsewhere only where it carries meaning.
The frame recesses; content sits raised on it.
Figtree for the product, JetBrains Mono for code, weights 400 and 500 only.
A spacing ladder measured off the reference comps, not a 4px grid.
Solar bold-duotone icons, linear only for chevrons and arrows.
Motion that keeps one object on screen through every change and exits faster than it enters.

rules.name: The No Ease-In Rule
rules.body: No ease-in curve exists, and no run starts slow: anything that starts slow feels like the interface hesitating.

rules.name: The Frequency Rule
rules.body: How often the reader sees a motion decides whether it exists. A keyboard-initiated action never animates; the same action from a pointer keeps its motion (typing is not an action). What is seen tens of times a day (a hover, a row's highlight) gets a colour or opacity change on `--dur-control` or nothing; what is occasional (a popover, a sheet, a toast) gets the standard motion; delight belongs only to what is rare. Motion is never the only sign that something happened.

rules.name: The Fast Exit Rule
rules.body: Exits are shorter than entrances, and a thing leaves the way it came: in over `--dur-pop` or `--dur-panel`, out over `--dur-exit`; a grown surface in over `--dur-grow`, out over `--dur-grow-exit`. Nothing outlasts `--dur-panel` but a message lifted between its bubble and the field (`--dur-lift`), a grown surface and the two picked recipes; ambient loops are not beats.

rules.name: The Enter Rule
rules.body: Nothing appears from nothing. A surface arrives from `--pop-scale` or `--pop-rise` short of its place, fading in, from its trigger's side (a dialog rises `--pop-rise`); every travel is `--pop-rise`, and a view handing its place along a strip comes `--swap-nudge` from its side. A press scales to `--press-scale`. Entrances and exits are `transform` and `opacity` (a `clip-path` where a box opens out of another, `height` only for a disclosure), and no keyframe writes a length (lint `house/no-raw-motion`). The tooltip is the one exception, because it is seen tens of times a day (The Frequency Rule): it fades in over `--dur-fade` settling `--tip-rise` toward its trigger, and leaves at once.

rules.name: The One Object Rule
rules.body: What is on both sides of a change travels; it never vanishes on one side and appears on the other (`motion/share.svelte.ts`). A flight runs `--dur-panel` on the drawer curve as a transform or a clip from the source's box, the source hidden meanwhile so the screen never shows two. A surface that closes on running work travels into the place that work is parked.

rules.name: The Nothing Jumps Rule
rules.body: When a list changes, rows that stay slide, rows that leave close while fading, and rows that arrive are uncovered while what follows makes room, all from one frame (`motion/rows.svelte.ts`). A move wholly off screen jumps, so nothing drifts into view behind the reader's scroll.

rules.name: The Interruptible Rule
rules.body: Every transition turns back from where it is drawn: a state a reader can flip twice in a second is a CSS transition on `data-state`, never a keyframe restarting from zero, and what a finger lets go of settles on the one spring with the finger's velocity (`motion/spring.ts`). Predetermined motion runs off the main thread.

rules.name: The Stay In Context Rule
rules.body: The reader stays where they are and knows what is true, from asking to done. Four questions shape every flow, and the weight of the decision sets its shape:

rules.name: The Open Page Rule
rules.body: Almost nothing blurs the page or stops the reader acting elsewhere. What asks or shows opens in the page beside what it concerns, and the rest stays live. The test: if they press something else now, does anything break? A scrim or a modal hold is for the rare moment when acting elsewhere would make the open question wrong.

rules.name: The Work Outlives Its Surface Rule
rules.body: Work a surface starts that runs longer than the surface stays open (an install, a spawn, an upload, a sign-in, an update) belongs to the work, and nothing the reader does to the page loses it.

rules.name: The Show Don't Tell Rule
rules.body: A fact with a shape is drawn, not written out: a schedule as times on a line, a budget as a meter, outcomes as marks in their status colours. Words are for what has no shape; a screen is designed as UI, never as a spreadsheet of its record.

rules.name: The One Loop Rule
rules.body: Anything that turns or blinks while pending runs `--dur-loop`, a rotation linear, a pulse ease-in-out; the skeleton's pulse is the one exception. Longer rhythms are multiples of the breath.

rules.name: The Steady Swap Rule
rules.body: A text swap never moves what stands beside it. Words change through MorphText (`components/ui/morph-text`): the box takes the larger of old and new at once and the new size once settled, so no width tweens. A label with a known second wording stands both in one cell as wide as the wider.

rules.name: The Reduced Motion Rule
rules.body: Motion is opt-in: every travelling transition sits under `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference`, and script asks `motionOk`. With reduced motion, fades still run and everything that travels lands; loops stop. Reduced motion means stillness, never an instant swap: what changed still fades.

rules.name: The House Helper Rule
rules.body: Each kind of motion has one helper, which already keeps the curves, clocks, interruption and reduced motion: `morph()` for a size change, `NsPopoverGroup` for sibling popovers, `reflow()` with `data-flip` for a list, `unfold` for a disclosure, `fluid-tabs` and the harness `Rail` for a switch, `keyed` for The Frequency Rule's keyboard half (`cawco/motion/`, `cawco/spawn/NsPopoverGroup.svelte`, `components/ui/fluid-tabs`, under `apps/dashboard/src/lib`). A component takes a one-clock composite (`transition-control`, …) rather than listing properties and clocks; a new pairing is a new token.

rules.name: The Quiet Feel Rule
rules.body: Sound and touch accompany a gesture the reader is making; they never announce anything, never stand in for a word or a glyph, and never play for something the reader did not do. Sound is Cuelume, synthesized, always at its `subtle` emphasis, off until the reader turns it on (the Sound switch beside the theme in the rail's footer, kept per browser, `feel.svelte.ts`). Touch is web-haptics, for a finger on a coarse pointer only, with no setting. Both load on the first press or key, never with the page, and warm up while idle so the first cue costs no frame.

rules.name: The Dark Flips Polarity Rule
rules.body: At night a groove sits below the card and a thumb above it. Dark mode is a second set of lightness decisions, never an inverted light mode.

rules.name: The Reserved Hue Rule
rules.body: Crimson, spark yellow, olive and blue mean status, and status only. Progress rings, identity and decoration take `currentColor` or an identity hue. A finished task ring is the one decoration that earns a state colour, because by then it is a result.

rules.name: The Coral Is Where You Act Rule
rules.body: Coral marks the action (one per view: the act the view is for, so a view for deciding spends it on the decision), the selected nav row, the focus ring, checked controls, the chosen option, the selection tint, and the vermillion rule that parts two regions of a glass card (Files, Caw's panel). Advice is never coral: a recommended option wears the Recommended badge, and when it starts chosen it wears both, so moving the pick moves only the coral. Coral is never a status, so it never reads as an alarm and an alarm never reads as a button.

rules.name: The White On Coral Rule
rules.body: Text on coral sits on `action-solid` or `chip-chosen-bg`, never on `brand-solid`. A new coral fill under text is measured to 4.5:1, top gradient stop included, before it ships.

rules.name: The Ink Stays Ink Rule
rules.body: Tooltips and inverted tiles are `ink-solid` with `on-ink`. They are never coral.

rules.name: The Idle Has No Fill Rule
rules.body: An idle session carries no chip. A quiet row means a healthy row, so rest is drawn as nothing.

rules.name: The No Indigo Rule
rules.body: Indigo is never a brand, action or accent hue. Identity hues span the wheel for telling things apart and are never promoted to a brand role.

rules.name: The Glyph, Word, Hue Rule
rules.body: Status is never colour alone. It reads glyph, then word, then hue (a Solar duotone glyph, then "Working", "Needs you", "Failed", "Idle", "Sleeping", "Stopped" or "Unreachable"). A mark that changes state changes shape as well as colour, and a chip carries the word inside its tint.

rules.name: The 500 Ceiling Rule
rules.body: No product text goes above 500. Emphasis is a step from 400 to 500 or an ink step, never bold.

rules.name: The Role, Not Size Rule
rules.body: Text takes a role by what it does: names, headings, column heads and badges are label; sentences are body; timestamps, counts, units and hints are meta. Nobody picks a size and finds a role for it.

rules.name: The Tabular Figure Rule
rules.body: A figure that changes carries `.num` and is set in tabular numerals, so a ticking value never moves its neighbours; tables are tabular by default.

rules.name: The Truncate Inside Rule
rules.body: Text truncates in an inner span, never on the control or link, so the hit area is never clipped; in a row the name gives way first.

rules.name: The Row Dress Rule
rules.body: A list row has at most four dresses: its name in label and `ink-row`; the thing itself (a comment's words, a message) in body and `ink-strong`; facts about it in meta and `ink-muted`; an unread fact in `ink-strong`. A state the row's mark draws takes no word, and the name carries the row's one weight step.

rules.name: The Mark Line Rule
rules.body: Words beside a mark (an icon, a dot, an avatar, a keycap) have their x-height's middle on the mark's middle, within half a pixel, in every engine. The mark line recipe (app.css) trims each run to its x-height band and pads the room back; the kit's rows draw it, any other row takes `.mark-line`, a box on the line says `data-box`, and a mark beside wrapping words sits in a `.mark-cell`. `apps/dashboard/scripts/mark-line-check.ts` enforces it.

rules.name: The 16px Field Rule
rules.body: On a coarse pointer every text field renders at 16px or more, because iOS Safari zooms into a smaller field.

rules.name: The Title Bars Follow Liquid Glass Rule
rules.body: Every bar that heads a surface (the top bar, a pane, a side panel, a sheet, a canvas's band) follows Apple's toolbar model as Liquid Glass revised it (HIG, Toolbars, 2025-12-16), on web and native:

rules.name: The Row Grid Rule
rules.body: A row's mark is centred in a 28px lead column, its words start on one text column `space-3` after it, and its last control ends on one trailing edge `space-3` in from the list's, drawn in ink: its last painted pixel (a fill, a ghost's last letter or stroke) lands on the edge within 1px, its box hanging past by what its ink stops short, never past the row's `space-3`, so a list never scrolls sideways.

rules.name: The Frame Recesses Rule
rules.body: The frame recesses and content never does. The one sanctioned card-in-card is the stat tile's recessed well.

rules.name: The Warm Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are warm ink taken from the neutral ramp, never `rgba(0,0,0,·)`. The tile's night drop is the one black, under a ring of ink.

rules.name: The Night Ring Rule
rules.body: At night a raised surface is told apart from its frame by a 1px inner ring of ink as well as its drop. The ring is part of the shadow token, so a component that takes the token gets it in both schemes.

rules.name: The Concentric Rule
rules.body: A surface nested in another's corner takes the outer radius less the gap between their edges, the outer's edge counted. Where no radius token is the derived value, a derived token holds it (`inner-well-r`), never a literal. A container declares its outer radius and inset once (design.css `concentric-in`) and its rows and parts take the result (`concentric-<radius>`); the hover ghost, the selection pill and the focus ring take the contour of what they mark.

rules.name: The Glass Contour Rule
rules.body: A control standing in a bar's glass takes the glass's contour by where it stands: its corners facing the capsule's ends take the capsule's radius less the pad, those facing a neighbour `radius-xs` (BarGlass marks each item leading, middle, trailing or only; design.css `concentric-row`). Hover, pressed, selected and focus are drawn on that one box (`concentric-at`), the ring inside it, so every state shares its contour; `state-shape` forces and reads each.

rules.name: The Measured Exception Rule
rules.body: The stat tile keeps the comp's radii (a card round its well), a panel its shell, and the smallest marks the hair. Each is a token.

rules.name: The Whole Pixel Border Rule
rules.body: A border or outline is a whole CSS pixel; a fractional stroke is an inset ring (`inset-ring-(length:--x)`) or an SVG stroke. `scripts/border-width-check.ts` refuses a fractional width.

rules.name: The Earned Count Rule
rules.body: A count on a control is drawn only above 0: at 0 the count element is gone and the control's name drops it too, on the web and in the app. A figure whose 0 is itself the reading (a measurement, a share, a total) is not a count.

rules.name: The Press Rule
rules.body: A compact standalone control (a button, a chip, a switch) scales to `--press-scale`; anything wide or grouped (rows, cards, tabs, segments), and any control that opens a list, menu or card, tints to `surface-pressed` and moves nothing. A link dims. The tint outranks a control's own fill by specificity, never `!important`.

rules.name: The Hold-To-Select Rule
rules.body: A press that starts in a text field is never captured by a drawer or gesture round it, so iOS hold-to-select and Paste reach the field. A held press on a context-menu trigger suppresses the platform callout.

rules.name: The Empty Starts Work Rule
rules.body: An empty state always offers to start the work that would fill it: its one action starts a session with Caw (or the screen's own agent) already asking for the thing, its words editable before they go. Where that can't start, it says why and offers the way by hand.

rules.name: The Caw Stands On The Axis Rule
rules.body: Caw sits in the 28px lead column only on a row. Everywhere else (an empty page, a hero, a setup card, a fault at a surface's centre) he stands centred on the composition's own axis.

rules.name: The Claim Of Nothing Rule
rules.body: An empty state renders only once the data is known to be empty. While it loads, the skeleton stands at the real layout's size, and the first read replaces it in the reveal. Nothing claims zero while the hub connection is down.

rules.name: The Real Wait Rule
rules.body: Nothing stands in for a wait until it has lasted `--dur-wait-grace`. Caw, once he appears, finishes his enter before what arrives lands, then fades out from the drawing he is on (assets/mascot/README.md, Contract).

rules.name: The Solar Duotone Rule
rules.body: Every product icon is Solar's bold-duotone cut, imported through `$lib/icons.ts` (packages/icons); a bar's symbols, chevrons, arrows and CopyButton take Solar's linear cut (`…Linear`, house/bar-symbol-linear). The duotone's second layer is `currentColor` at 50%. A status glyph keeps its `status-*-glyph` hue and holds 3:1 as a whole on its surfaces. Close, Plus and Tick are local glyphs on Solar's 24px grid, a 1.5 stroke with round caps; the Tick is also the done glyph, in `status-done-glyph`. An icon is the glyph alone, no container round it; where Solar ships only a contained cut, a bare one is drawn in its style.

rules.name: The Caret Rule
rules.body: A text field's focus indicator is its caret (WCAG 2.2 Understanding 2.4.7): no field, editor or search strip draws the coral ring. A field with a frame steps that frame's edge to `border-control-strong` while its text has focus (`field-edge`); a field that is the whole surface shows its caret alone.

rules.name: The One Ring Rule
rules.body: Every control shows one ring on keyboard focus only (`:focus-visible`): a 2px outline in `focus-ring`, 2px outside, never a box-shadow, so it follows the radius and survives forced colours; inset on rows, tabs and anything flush or clipped. The ring is for focus alone: a selection or a mode takes the selected marks instead.

rules.name: The 44 Touch Rule
rules.body: On a coarse pointer every control's tappable area reaches 44×44 through a transparent `::after` (`.touch-hit`) while its drawn size stays; neighbours stop at the midpoint (`--hit-gap-x`, `--hit-gap-y`). A text field's area lies under it (`.hit-under`). A chip in running text takes its line's height, as a link does (WCAG 2.5.8's inline exception).

rules.name: The 24 Pointer Rule
rules.body: On a fine pointer a control drawn under 24×24 reaches 24px through `.pointer-hit`.

rules.name: The Peer Rule
rules.body: Approve and Deny are peers on every surface that answers a permission (Caw's panel, the transcript's card `transcript/Prompt.svelte`, the peek): the operator answers under time pressure, often from a phone, and a rushed thumb must not grant when it meant deny. They are the same size (`sm`, with a 44×44 hit area on every pointer), the same label type, the same `surface-recess` fill and `border-button-outline` edge, in `ink-strong`, reading apart by glyph, word and place, never by hue; no status fill or ink touches either, and neither changes under the pointer. They stand at opposite ends of their row, at least `--space-8` apart, with no third control between them.

rules.name: The Consequential Grant Rule
rules.body: A standing grant ("Always allow … for …") is wider than the request, so it is kept apart: under a break and a hairline, after a sentence saying what it would allow, in the warning tint with warning ink, a shield glyph and a real edge, the most salient control on the card on purpose. Above the answer row the card says who asks, what will happen and to what, and the change itself, open (the diff, scrolling inside). Nothing is behind a disclosure: a grant is made on what it changes.

rules.name: The Should It Exist Rule
rules.body:
Before a string is phrased, it earns its place on the screen (the `clean-copy` skill). Walk it down in order and cut at the first that fires: a thing the person would never have wondered about, unprompted, goes, since naming it plants the question; a caption that restates its label, field or value goes; a line that rules out a failure, defends a choice or remembers a fixed bug goes (the fix is the fix). Cut whole clauses; when nothing is left, the element goes with its words, its empty hint prop and its `

` too.

dos: Do take every visual value from the tokens, adding a token before any one-off value.
Do check every change in both schemes, at 1440 and 390.
Do keep one coral act per view, and say status by glyph and word before hue.
Do carry shared objects across a change and take the house helper for each motion.
Do shape each flow by The Stay In Context Rule and open it in the page.
Do put a decision about one screen in that screen's surface brief, and a change to the system here.
donts: Don't use coral for a status, a status hue for an action or decoration, or indigo anywhere.
Don't set text above 500, on `brand-solid`, or under 16px in a field on a coarse pointer.
Don't use an ease-in curve, animate a keyboard action, or let an exit outlast its entrance.
Don't tell a failure in a toast, or lose work a surface started.
Don't ship copy that fails The Should It Exist Rule.

Don't use a `group-has-*` utility in the dashboard: one such rule makes every element put into the page restyle the whole rail. Style from a state the component sets on itself or its group (`group-data-*`), or a sibling.
